findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top convergence gene: up in UC biopsies (meta-analysis [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.264]) with Open Targets genetic support and an overall UC association [gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.5345]. Small-molecule tractability is 'SM: Advanced Clinical' and drugs include reparixin (PHASE_3) and navarixin, ladarixin, danirixin, elubrixin and SX-682 (PHASE_2), none a UC indication in the returned records; Reactome places it in neutrophil degranulation and chemokine receptor signalling.

CXCL8 is strongly induced in all cohorts ([gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.704]) but has no Open Targets genetic association with UC (genetics component zero); clinical-stage anti-IL-8 antibodies exist (ABX-IL8, adakitug, PHASE_2). STRING links CXCR2 to CXCL8 at very high confidence, supporting an IL-8/CXCR2 neutrophil axis driven by expression and literature rather than genetics.

CXCR1 shares the same clinical dual CXCR1 and CXCR2 inhibitors as CXCR2 (reparixin PHASE_3, ladarixin, navarixin, SX-682 PHASE_2) and has intermediate Open Targets genetic support; it is up in biopsies in the same direction across five cohorts. STRING links it to CXCR2 at high confidence.

CHI3L1 has among the largest biopsy changes ([gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.714]) and strong replication, but no Open Targets genetic support and no drug in the returned records; it fits a biomarker or mechanism role, not a drug target.

JAK2 has the second-highest Open Targets UC association among the known targets ([gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7318]) yet changes only modestly in biopsies ([gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.872]); genetically supported but not strongly expression-led. Fedratinib is approved (in another indication).

OSMR is up in UC ([gene=OSMR; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.042]) with genetic association and an antibody tractability label 'AB: Advanced Clinical'; vixarelimab (PHASE_2) is the only drug returned. Reactome: IL-6-type cytokine receptor ligand interactions. OSM itself is not among the top 1999 Open Targets UC associations.

IDO1 is strongly up ([gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.445]) without genetic association; drugs returned are epacadostat (APPROVAL stage as listed) and linrodostat (PHASE_3), in other indications.

Established target IL23R has strong genetic association ([gene=IL23R; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.5997]) but is absent from the stored convergence ranking, so biopsy expression does not single it out. The same holds for TNF; known-target status comes from genetics and drugs, not from the transcriptomic signal.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in five cohorts and has genetic association; marketed PD-L1 antibodies (atezolizumab PHASE_4, sugemalimab APPROVAL) exist in oncology only, so repurposing is not supported and checkpoint agonism rather than blockade would be the relevant direction.

MMP1, MMP3, MMP7, MMP9 and MMP10 are all up with consistent replication and none has Open Targets genetic support; broad MMP inhibitors (marimastat PHASE_3) exist, but this family is better read as a tissue-damage biomarker set than a validated target.

CXCL1, CXCL5 and S100A8/S100A9 are strongly replicated up-regulated genes with no returned drugs and no genetic association; STRING links CXCL1 and CXCL5 to CXCR2 at very high confidence, reinforcing the neutrophil chemokine axis.
IL2RA is up with genetic association and has drugs (basiliximab PHASE_4, other agents) in other indications; its expression change is modest relative to the chemokine and MMP genes.

caveats: Drug stages are Open Targets maximum clinical stage in any indication, not UC trials.
Bulk biopsy changes may reflect infiltrating neutrophils and myeloid cells rather than epithelial change.
IL23R and TNF are outside the stored convergence top, so their expression behaviour was not quantified.
PubMed connector was unavailable (needs authorization); no extra literature checks.
